project.subtitle: An Auditable Clinical Prediction Laboratory
project.title: Feature Selection and Scratch Optimization for Clinical Prediction
project.purpose: Compare dimensionality reduction and first-principles optimization on two reproducible clinical datasets while exposing every training signal and evaluation decision.
project.author: Divya
project.institution: Indira Gandhi Delhi Technical University for Women

regression.name: Diabetes progression
regression.role: One-variable OLS and batch gradient descent

research_questions: How much classification performance is retained when 30 tumour descriptors are reduced to 10?
Does batch gradient descent converge to the same one-variable linear solution as analytical OLS?
Can a scratch logistic model remain competitive across statistically, recursively, and tree-selected feature subsets?

limitations: The datasets are educational benchmarks and do not represent deployment-ready clinical validation.
RFE and embedded selection are fit on training data only, but a single held-out split cannot quantify all sampling uncertainty.
The one-feature regression task is intentionally interpretable and does not claim to be the strongest possible diabetes predictor.
The application is an explanatory research interface, not a diagnostic device.
